Agreed on deliverables and preliminary timeline for December/January pilot prep.
transcript:
Meeting Header: 2026-12-07 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~55m
Attendees: Maria Chen (Redwood AE), Tejas Patel (Redwood SE), Lina Gomez (Redwood Product), Aiden Ross (OrionCloud Head Partnerships), Priya Narayan (OrionCloud Cloud Integrations), Samir Khan (OrionCloud Security), Hannah Lee (OrionCloud Marketplace PM)

00:00 Maria Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we'll keep this to 45 ish minutes plus q&a, super excited to align on the marketplace listing and a reference architecture for the joint solution
00:18 Aiden Ross: thanks Maria, yeah we want to make sure the listing meets our marketplace requirements and that the integration is trivial for our customers, also want notes for procurement folks
00:30 Maria Chen: today Tejas will walk through deployment options and the ref arch, Lina will talk go-to-market blurb and listing metadata, then open for sec questions with Samir
00:44 Tejas Patel: cool, i'll share my screen  quick disclaimer, i'll be using shorthand for some product names, so Redwood Dedicated means our reserved capacity offering, Redwood Private is VPC/on-prem variant, and Console is the observability panel, ok?
00:58 Priya Narayan: yep, that's the mapping we had in the doc, though some internal teams call it Broker or Gateway, so keep both terms available in the listing
01:10 Tejas Patel: great. so at a high level  three integration patterns we recommend for OrionCloud customers: 1) Hosted API integration  easiest, low friction, ideal for pilots and PLG; 2) Dedicated pools we can provision in OrionCloud's marketplace offering with committed capacity and guaranteed throughput; 3) Private/VPC deployment for regulated customers with VPC peering or private link  supports KMS/HSM and audit logs.
01:35 Hannah Lee: for marketplace, we usually prefer the dedicated listing if there is any guaranteed SLA, because we can surface that, but also having a hosted quick-start tile helps adoption
01:46 Tejas Patel: yes exactly, we typically include both: a hosted tile for self-serve signups and a marketplace-enabled dedicated SKU for customers wanting guaranteed capacity and billing through OrionCloud. The ref arch will show both paths.
02:02 Aiden Ross: can you share what the ref arch doc will include  network diagrams, IAM, certs  what's the BOM?
02:12 Tejas Patel: we'll include: network topology diagrams (VPC peering vs private link), inbound/outbound rules, load balancing / routing for inference endpoints, KMS/HSM integration points for model keys and data encryption, RBAC mapping to OrionCloud IAM, and optional on-prem agent for air-gapped installs. Also a list of infra components like GPU types, storage for model weights, expected IOPS, and estimated monthly cost ranges.
02:36 Samir Khan: on KMS  does Redwood support customer-managed keys in a HSM? We need to ensure keys never leave our control for regulated workloads
02:44 Tejas Patel: yes  Redwood Private supports KMS/HSM integrations; we have instructions for AWS KMS, Google KMS, and for HSM via PKCS11 flows. We'll include a sample flow: model artifacts encrypted at rest, keys managed by customer, and Redwood's control plane only sees wrapped keys.
03:01 Samir Khan: ok good, also need to see audit log fields  token-level request ids, user mapping, model version, prompt hash  for our SIEM ingestion
03:12 Lina Gomez: we'll populate the audit sample schema in the ref arch doc; Redwood Console emits logs and traces and you can export via S3/CloudWatch or syslog to your SIEM.
03:25 Priya Narayan: great, and billing  for dedicated SKU, do we support marketplace consolidated billing so the customer pays via OrionCloud?
03:32 Maria Chen: yes, marketplace billing is supported; we can do a metered/subscription SKU and OrionCloud invoicing. We'll share the billing integration guide.
03:42 Hannah Lee: onboarding steps for the listing  we need metadata: product description, thumbnails, SLA text, supported regions, minimum commit, deployment options, links to security docs, and a reference arch PDF. Also a staging marketplace account for verification.
03:58 Maria Chen: noted. we'll prepare that metadata; Lina will draft the blurb and we can iterate.
04:05 Tejas Patel: i want to call out a couple of caveats: for high throughput inference (real-time), we recommend using Dedicated with the GPU types we tested  A100s or equivalent  and enabling our batching + KV caching. For embeddings or async workloads, hosted is usually fine.
04:24 Aiden Ross: do you have benchmarks we can publish on the listing? our marketplace prefers some indicative numbers
04:31 Tejas Patel: we can share anonymized benchmarks and a small benchmark harness. for example, 16k-token seq throughput on A100 with q4 quantization shows X latency/throughput  i'll prepare a sanitized table. note that numbers vary by model and payload.
04:49 Priya Narayan: can we run a joint pilot where we provision a dedicated pool in a staging region and run our sample workloads?
04:56 Tejas Patel: absolutely  propose Jan week 2 for the pilot. we'll need a list of models, typical prompt lengths, and target RR99 latency/SLOs.
05:06 Samir Khan: security checklist: SOC2 docs, ISO, pen test, SSO/SAML, SCIM, RBAC mappings, data residency, key lifecycle, and breach notification SLA  can you send those?
05:18 Maria Chen: yes  we'll attach SOC2 and ISO artifacts, SSO/SAML integration guide, and a short security note for the marketplace listing. expect those by Dec 10.
05:29 Aiden Ross: good. on the reference arch  we also want a short 'how it works' animation or annotated diagram for the marketplace tile  customers click, see a simple flow, and then can request dedicated provisioning
05:40 Lina Gomez: we can produce a one-page diagram and an animated gif for the tile, and a longer 6-8 page ref arch for tech leads.
05:50 Hannah Lee: also for marketplace compliance we require a short demo video under 2 minutes  could Redwood supply that?
05:57 Maria Chen: yes we can provide a demo video and a short set of screenshots from Console and the onboarding flow.
06:06 Priya Narayan: ok, switching to integration details  VPC peering vs private link  which do you recommend for OrionCloud customers?
06:14 Tejas Patel: both are supported. for lower latency and when both sides control routing, VPC peering is straightforward. For more managed control and cross-account access we recommend private link. We'll include step-by-step for both. Note: private link requires an endpoint service setup on Redwood's side and some marketplace wiring.
06:34 Aiden Ross: any special ports or NAT requirements? some of our customers are strict
06:39 Tejas Patel: only outbound TLS 443 to control plane for health checks; inference traffic is inside VPC/private link. We'll include exact firewall rules and ephemeral port ranges in the doc.
06:53 Samir Khan: what about model artifacts  will they be pulled from S3 in our account or pushed?
06:59 Tejas Patel: we support pulling from a customer's storage (S3/GCS) with a signed role, or Redwood can host model weights in encrypted storage for dedicated pools. We'll show both patterns and trade-offs (control vs ease).
07:16 Aiden Ross: great. on marketplace listing taxonomy  which categories should we set? 'AI inference', 'Machine Learning Platforms', 'Developer Tools'?
07:23 Lina Gomez: suggested tags: "LLM Inference", "Model Serving", "Embeddings", "Marketplace Integration", and add 'Compliance-ready' for the private offering. We'll draft.
07:34 Hannah Lee: also need a short list of supported regions per SKU. can you provide region coverage?
07:40 Tejas Patel: listed regions: us-west-2, us-east-1, eu-west-1, ap-southeast-1 (pilot limited). We'll confirm capacity windows for dedicated SKUs.
07:50 Priya Narayan: dependencies  do we rely on OrcaNet or other third-party infra that might conflict with our partner requirements?
07:55 Maria Chen: not directly; Redwood runtime uses standard cloud GPUs and some open-source libs. we'll enumerate third-party dependencies and licenses in the ref arch.
08:04 Aiden Ross: competitors  we noticed CloudPeak and NovaEdge show similar marketplace listings; how do we position vs them?
08:12 Maria Chen: we emphasize production economics and unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private, plus very developer-friendly console and rollout controls. We'll provide a short competitive matrix for the partner portal.
08:25 Samir Khan: operationally  who owns first-line support for marketplace-billed customers?
08:31 Maria Chen: initial triage handled by Redwood Support; for dedicated enterprise customers we can enable a joint escalation matrix and optionally co-branded support. We'll include a sample SLO table.
08:44 Priya Narayan: ok logistics  what repo or artifact will you upload for us to review?
08:49 Tejas Patel: we'll push a draft reference arch PDF, the marketplace metadata JSON, and a staging listing screenshots to a shared S3 link. I'll create the link and send via email.
09:00 Aiden Ross: perfect. last part  go-to-market cadence and PR: Hannah you had asked about joint announcement windows?
09:08 Hannah Lee: yes ideally after the pilot and once marketplace listing is validated. we're thinking Q1 launch; we'll sync on a joint press timeline and co-marketing assets.
09:18 Lina Gomez: Lina here, i'll draft a one pager for partner portal and a short partner playbook with sample customer messaging.
09:26 Maria Chen: cool  to recap next steps: Maria to send security docs by Dec 10; Lina to prepare listing blurb and joint solution description by Dec 16; Tejas to ready benchmark harness and pilot plan by Dec 22; Priya to send marketplace metadata and logos by Dec 11; all to reconvene after docs are shared.
09:46 Aiden Ross: sounds good  quick Q from Samir: do you support SCIM for user provisioning?
09:52 Tejas Patel: yes, SCIM and SAML available  we'll include sample config.
09:58 Samir Khan: and vulnerability disclosure process?
10:02 Maria Chen: we have a security contact and vulnerability policy; will include an ingress for security reports and expected timelines.
10:10 Hannah Lee: ok thanks everyone. i'll wait for artifacts and we'll aim to get listing into staging by Dec 20 if possible
10:20 Maria Chen: thanks all, appreciate the time  we'll follow up with the links and calendar invites for the pilot.

Transcript Notes: occasional transcription artifacts: 'KV cache' heard as 'kay vee cache', 'VPC peering' sometimes 'VPC pairing' in the text. Speaker labels may be imperfect in some automated export segments. Links referenced: 'shared S3 link (to be provided)', 'marketplace metadata template (OrionCloud portal)'.

End of call.
